contribution: Transformer architecture and large-scale pre-training establish the parametric-knowledge paradigm; FEVER frames fact verification as a retrieval-plus-inference task.
impact: Sets up the assumption that knowledge lives in weights - the assumption the rest of this decade spends undoing.

contribution: LAMA probing shows LMs recall substantial relational knowledge but unevenly and with high prompt sensitivity.
impact: Establishes empirically that parametric memory is real but unreliable, motivating external retrieval.

contribution: DPR replaces lexical matching with learned dense retrieval; REALM trains retrieval jointly during pre-training; RAG unifies a dense retriever with a generative reader end to end.
impact: The founding year of RAG. Knowledge becomes modular and swappable rather than frozen in weights.

contribution: Fusion-in-Decoder scales evidence aggregation across many passages; retrieval augmentation is shown to reduce hallucination in dialogue; FAISS makes billion-scale vector search practical.
impact: First direct evidence that retrieval reduces hallucination specifically, plus the infrastructure that makes deployment feasible.

contribution: RETRO demonstrates trillion-token retrieval lets small models match much larger ones; TruthfulQA shows scale can worsen truthfulness.
impact: Decouples knowledge from parameter count and shows scaling alone does not solve factuality - inverse scaling on truthfulness.

contribution: Retrieval becomes adaptive and iterative - FLARE retrieves on low confidence, IRCoT interleaves retrieval with reasoning; black-box methods (REPLUG, In-Context RALM) work without model access; SelfCheckGPT and FActScore make hallucination measurable; adaptive retrieval is justified by long-tail analysis.
impact: The pivot year: retrieval shifts from a fixed pre-processing step to a decision the model makes during generation, and hallucination becomes quantifiable.

contribution: Self-reflection and correction enter the pipeline (Self-RAG, CRAG, Chain-of-Verification); structure enters the index (GraphRAG, RAPTOR); evaluation matures (RAGAS, RGB, RAGTruth); 'Lost in the Middle' and semantic entropy expose context and uncertainty limits.
impact: RAG stops being a pipeline and becomes a control loop with verification. Evaluation shifts from end-to-end accuracy to component-wise diagnosis.

contribution: Theoretical limits are formalised (hallucination shown to be innate; incentive analysis of why models guess); agentic RAG surveys consolidate multi-step tool-using retrieval; peer-reviewed journal syntheses and controlled variant comparisons appear.
impact: The field matures from technique proliferation to consolidation, and accepts that elimination is not achievable - the goal becomes bounded, measurable residual risk.

contribution: Industrial deployment studies and automated hallucination corpus construction move the work from benchmarks to production and from manual to scalable annotation.
impact: Evidence base shifts from laboratory benchmarks to operational reporting, exposing the gap between benchmark and production performance.
